items.title: How Tripo Is Tackling Clean Topology for its 3D Asset Pipeline
items.excerpt: Tripo co-founder Dr. Yanpei Cao explains Smart Mesh, which generates usable topology in seconds, and how the company is shifting from single generated assets toward production-ready, editable 3D for complete interactive worlds.
items.why: Generated 3D has been unusable downstream because of messy topology; if AI output arrives retopo-ready, the 3D artist's cleanup step disappears from the pipeline.

items.title: The power of on-premises open-weight models for generative media
items.excerpt: A look at adopting open-weight generative AI models on-premises, and how local deployment improves workflow stability, security, cost predictability, and delivery for creative studios.
items.why: Studios that can't send client footage to a cloud API get a real answer: run the model in-house. It changes who can adopt generative media at all.

items.title: "Unsettling" – Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 AI filter has leaked, and gamers are horrified
items.excerpt: An early build of Nvidia's DLSS 5 neural rendering filter has leaked, and the AI-repainted look it applies over game frames is dividing artists and players.
items.why: A driver-level AI filter can overwrite art direction after the artist has shipped it — the first real fight over who owns the final look of a rendered frame.

items.title: The $3.4m Disney auction is a reminder of what AI concept art takes from us
items.excerpt: A record-breaking auction of original Disney concept art becomes an argument about what disappears when concept work is generated rather than drawn.
items.why: Concept art is the first craft AI fully absorbed; this puts a price tag on the artifact-and-provenance side designers are trading away.

items.title: If Apple and Spotify are cracking down on AI slop, why can't YouTube?
items.excerpt: Apple and Spotify have started policing AI-generated filler on their platforms while YouTube has not — an argument about why the incentives differ.
items.why: Platform slop policy decides whether human-made creative work still surfaces — distribution rules are now part of a designer's craft economics.

items.title: Run Claude Managed Agents with Chat SDK
items.excerpt: Vercel shows how to ship a Slack research bot on Claude Managed Agents and the Chat SDK: one persistent session per thread, streamed briefs with sources, and no Slack credentials to manage.
items.why: Agent UI is becoming a template you assemble, not a product you design from scratch — the interface layer for agents is getting commoditized.

items.title: Hy4 Preview now available on AI Gateway
items.excerpt: Tencent's Hy4 Preview can now be called through Vercel AI Gateway with a single API key — no provider account, with automatic fallbacks, spend tracking and per-request traces.
items.why: Model choice keeps collapsing into one key behind a gateway, so swapping the engine under a design tool stops being an engineering project.

items.title: Structuring Variables in Figma
items.excerpt: A practical scheme for organising Figma variables — primitives, semantic aliases, collections and modes — so a UI library stays scalable as projects grow.
items.why: A named, closed set of variables is exactly what keeps a generating agent from inventing values — token structure is now the guardrail, not the housekeeping.

items.title: A Measurement-First Workflow for Evaluating AI Interior Concepts
items.excerpt: AI image systems produce plausible interiors that quietly break real dimensions; this proposes measuring the generated concept against the actual room before anyone falls in love with the render.
items.why: Generated concepts look buildable and aren't; putting measurement before taste is the missing review step for AI visualisation.

items.title: Designing An AI 3D Logo Maker Around Two Clear Input Contracts
items.excerpt: The argument that the most consequential decision in an AI 3D logo tool isn't the model picker but the input contract — what the user is allowed to hand the system, and in what shape.
items.why: For generative design tools the real design work has moved to the input surface — what you constrain up front determines the output more than the model does.

items.title: Source Material: i-D Magazine's Editor in Chief Is Not Afraid of Visual Chaos
items.excerpt: Thom Bettridge walks through the magazines that shaped his taste and the design rules he breaks most often, in Figma's Source Material series.
items.why: As tools converge on the same clean defaults, a working editor's case for deliberate visual chaos is the counterweight designers need.

items.title: The Making of i-D Magazine's 375 "The Beta Issue" — Designed in Figma
items.excerpt: Thom Bettridge shares the inspiration and process behind i-D Magazine's 375 "The Beta Issue," taking the phrase "youth culture magazine" as literally as possible — laid out in Figma.
items.why: A print magazine built in a product-design tool shows how far Figma has drifted from UI into general-purpose art direction.

items.title: The Unlock | Product Mockups with Badal Patel
items.excerpt: Badal Patel of Super Spicy studio walks through his product-mockup approach, combining Adobe Firefly generation with hands-on Photoshop work.
items.why: A working graphic designer showing exactly where he lets Firefly in and where he doesn't — the practical division of labour, not the pitch.

items.title: As VR Gaming Looks for New Footing, the Out-of-Home XR Entertainment Space is Still Building
items.excerpt: With consumer VR gaming unsettled, investment and development attention is shifting to location-based XR attractions as the next viable design space.
items.why: Where XR money goes decides what XR designers get to make; venue-scale experiences are a very different design brief from headset apps.

items.title: Meta Is Working To Spin Off Worlds From The Horizon Mobile App
items.excerpt: Datamining suggests Meta is preparing to split Horizon Worlds into its own mobile app, leaving the current Horizon app dedicated to XR headsets.
items.why: Splitting the app splits the design problem: a phone-first social world and a headset companion stop being able to share one interface.

items.title: This shirt is like an AI invisibility cloak
items.excerpt: Designer Simon Weckert's garment uses a deliberately wacky pattern that works as camouflage against AI vision systems.
items.why: Pattern design as a functional interface to machine perception — a concrete example of designing for the model as an audience.

items.title: How Apple made its charming claymation Mac mini ad
items.excerpt: Apple's new Mac mini spot was built entirely from physical materials — a claymation choice that says a lot about where its advertising is heading.
items.why: Handmade is becoming a signal: when generated imagery is free, visible physical craft is what an ad spends money to prove.
